newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Hyundai denies interest in Hanbo takeover.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Hyundai denies interest in Hanbo takeover.

text.p: A president of South Korea's giant Hyundai Group said his group was not interested in taking over troubled Hanbo Steel Co despite its interest in steelmaking, a group spokesman said on Tuesday.

"There is no change in our plan to enter (the) steelmaking business, but we don't have any intention of buying out Hanbo Steel," the spokesman quoted Park Se-yong, president of Hyundai Group's office for planning and coordination, as telling reporters.
Park said Hyundai was only interested in starting an integrated steel mill using furnaces but not in Hanbo's electric-arc furnace.
He also denied holding talks with the government and Hanbo's creditor banks over a possible takeover.
"We've had no discussions with the government, and creditor banks have not requested any negotiations," Park said.

Hyundai has repeatedly revealed its interest in setting up an integrated steel mill but the government has indirectly opposed the plan, citing problems of an oversupply and a concentration of economic power in one conglomerate.
Creditors of the failed Hanbo Steel have said they would sell the company in an open tender on July 8.
Hanbo Steel, the flagship of Hanbo Group, collapsed in January after piling up five trillion won in debt.
